transcript:
Meeting header:
Date/Time: 2027-08-09 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Avery Chen (Redwood AE); Samir Rao (Redwood SE); Elena Park (Redwood CSM); Dr. Maya Singh (Pinegrove CTO); Luis Ortega (IT Manager); Nora Patel (Product Lead); Sam Torres (Security)

Summary:
- Kickoff for Pinegrove Clinic onboarding to Redwood (hosted + exploring Dedicated/VPC for PHI).
- Discussed high-level timeline, success criteria for a pilot, security requirements (SSO, audit logs, KMS), and initial technical tasks (sandbox, network, model selection).
- Agreed next steps: share security docs, provision sandbox, schedule deep dive on networking and Dedicated sizing.

Topics: onboarding timeline; pilot success criteria; SSO/SAML; VPC/private deployment options; data retention and KMS; model choices and latency vs cost tradeoffs; next steps and owners.

Transcript:
[00:00] Avery: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Avery from Redwood, account exec, joined by Samir our solutions engineer and Elena our CSM. How's everybody doing?
[00:08] Maya: Good thanks, sorry for the slight delay, travel day.
[00:12] Luis: All good here.
[00:15] Avery: Great. Quick agenda - we want to cover scope and timeline for the pilot, security and compliance needs, network/topology options (VPC/on-prem), and then agree owners and next steps. Does that sound right?
[00:28] Nora: Yep that's exactly what we need. We're trying to get a pilot up within 3 weeks if possible.
[00:33] Avery: Okay 3 weeks - ambitious but doable for a basic hosted pilot. If we include Dedicated or VPC there might be a bit more lead time.
[00:41] Maya: Right, our big constraint is PHI - so if any PHI touches the system we need proper controls. At minimum SOC2, SSO, KMS for encryption, audit logs, and ideally VPC peering or on-prem for production. For pilot we can use de-identified data.
[00:56] Samir: Understood. We often start pilots on hosted but with tenant data de-id, then move to Dedicated or Private for prod. For PHI production we'd recommend Redwood Private with customer-managed KMS and VPC peering.
[01:09] Luis: When you say private, do you mean fully on-prem or a VPC option? Our security team prefers VPC peering into a private deployment so traffic doesn't go over the public internet.
[01:20] Samir: Exactly, we offer both: VPC peering into a customer VPC for private control plane, and an on-prem package if you need air-gapped. For pilot, VPC peering configuration can add a week or two depending on network approvals.
[01:34] Maya: Okay that helps, timeline wise if we want pilot in 3 weeks and keep it hosted with de-id data, that sounds ok. For production we'll aim for Private and KMS.
[01:43] Avery: Great. Nora, can you sketch success criteria for the pilot - what will show whether this is useful to product?
[01:51] Nora: Sure - two things: 1) model accuracy on our triage prompts hitting >= 85% on the labeled holdout, and 2) latency under 300ms p50 for short prompts in the UI. Also low error rates and stable throughput for 10 concurrent users.
[02:07] Samir: Good clear criteria. For latency 300ms p50, we should baseline with the model you intend to use. We can run a quick benchmark on our hosted profile or simulate on Dedicated. Depends on model and token lengths.
[02:20] Luis: About the model choices - we were looking at a smaller Llama variant and a mid-size open model. Concerned about cost if we run larger models in prod.
[02:30] Samir: Totally - there's the usual tradeoff of model size vs latency and cost. We can recommend quantization and batching to reduce unit cost. Redwood Optimize gives recommendations per workload; we'll share a quantization profile.
[02:43] Maya: Also, we need audit logs for every inference call with request metadata for compliance. Is that available?
[02:50] Elena: Yes, we have per-request logs and retention policies. For Private we can ship logs to your SIEM via secure forwarding, and for hosted there are configurable retention windows; we'll include that in the security pack.
[03:03] Samir: One caveat - very verbose logs can increase egress and storage costs, but it's straightforward to set policies.
[03:10] Luis: Noted. Samir, you mentioned KV cache earlier in documentation, can that be used across sessions?
[03:18] Samir: We use a KV cache for prefix reuse, it's designed to speed up repeated contexts, but for multi-tenant setups cache sharing is per-tenant; we won't mix customer data. Also for PHI we can disable persistent caches if you prefer.
[03:32] Nora: Good to know. For SSO - we use Okta for SAML 2.0, should be standard?
[03:39] Elena: Yes Okta SAML is supported. We'll share the SSO config guide. Also RBAC roles map to your groups.
[03:46] Sam Torres: From security side: do you support customer-managed keys (KMS) and HSM integration?
[03:52] Samir: Yes, for Private deployments we support CMKs via AWS KMS or customer HSM integration for on-prem. For hosted we have options for per-tenant envelope keys but full CMK control requires Private.
[04:05] Maya: Great. Pricing - what's the fastest way to get a Dedicated estimate for our expected throughput?
[04:11] Avery: We'll run sizing with Samir - if you share expected qps and expected percent production tokens we can recommend a Dedicated pool size and provide cost. For pilot we'll put a hosted baseline cost.
[04:21] Luis: We'll share traffic estimates after this call.
[04:24] Avery: Thanks. Next steps recap - we'll send security docs (SSO, SOC2, encryption), share pricing and Dedicated options, provision a sandbox account, and schedule a technical deep dive to align on VPC and network.
[04:36] Nora: One operational question - how do you handle model rollouts and canarying? We want to be able to A/B test model variants.
[04:45] Samir: Rollouts and canary deploys are built into the Console: route rules by percentage, fallback policies, and automatic rollback on error thresholds. We'll walk through that in the follow-up deep dive.
[04:57] Maya: Sounds good. For the pilot dataset, we will prepare a de-identified sample of 500 triage messages and the labeled holdout. Is that sufficient?
[05:06] Samir: That's perfect for an initial eval. We'll leverage that to run quality checks and compute baseline metrics.
[05:12] Elena: I'll create the sandbox workspace and invite your team, include a playbook for onboarding steps and API keys. You'll get a quickstart guide with Postman and Python examples.
[05:22] Luis: For networking - we have an internal firewall team who will need the IP ranges and cert details for peering. Is that something you can provide?
[05:29] Samir: Yes we'll provide IP ranges, TLS cert expectations, and a network checklist. For VPC peering we'll coordinate with your infra to map CIDR ranges and set up route tables.
[05:38] Maya: Any blockers on data residency? We need US-only hosting for PHI.
[05:43] Avery: We have US regions available; we can pin the deployment region. For Private deployments we can guarantee regional isolation.
[05:49] Nora: Ok great. One more thing - can the sandbox mimic our UI latency profile? We use short prompts but heavy attachments on the UI side.
[05:57] Samir: The sandbox can simulate token lengths and concurrency. Attachments are more about your pre-processing and upload pipeline; we can help with best practices but Redwood handles the inference side once the prompt is converted to text.
[06:10] Luis: Regarding compliance artifacts, we'll need an SOC2 attestation and a data processing agreement.
[06:16] Elena: We'll attach SOC2 and DPA in the security pack. Also SLA terms are in the enterprise agreement for Dedicated.
[06:24] Maya: Awesome. Anything else from your side?
[06:28] Avery: Not from me. We'll follow up with the docs and schedule the deep dive.
[06:32] Nora: Thanks everyone, looking forward to next steps.

[07:00] - end of recorded transcript (meeting ran ~45 minutes, this export truncates some back-and-forth but captures main items).

Notes on transcription quality: medium - some overlap and a few proper nouns mis-transcribed (e.g., internal project names), timestamps approximate.
